content.thinking: I should fix the wording here - rather than "half hour," I need to describe the error logging as occurring across the time range that overlaps the onset, noting the rate was still normal beforehand. Similarly for the other interval, I should clarify those errors only appeared during that window and not before it.

action_items.item: Before monthly-spend-feature is switched on again, run the new tests in tests/io_shop/test_spend_summary.py against the merged fix and require them to pass.
Roll out io-shop feature flags to a small share of shoppers first, and widen the rollout only while the account page error rate stays at its usual level.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed. The share of the service's requests that failed with server errors rose from {errors_before} before the onset to {errors_while_broken} on average while it was broken, and reached {errors_at_worst} at its worst.
Account page requests were raising ZeroDivisionError: division by zero at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py line {F1.2}. These errors were logged during {G5309.3}, and none were logged earlier.

ruled_out.what: A deploy. The search for production changes in the day before the onset found no deploys, and the flag toggle was the only change it found.
Another flag change. The flag provider's history showed only one flag change by anyone but Argus in the hour it read, and that change is this toggle.

Account page failures from shoppers closing the connection (ClientDisconnected). These were logged during {G46bc.3}, which includes the stretch before the onset when the error rate was at its usual level.

causal_chain.step: Account page requests started going down the monthly spend summary path because the feature flag monthly-spend-feature was switched on at {P1.1}. Before that, every flag evaluation came back off. In the minute it was switched, evaluations were mixed between off and on, and from the next minute every evaluation came back on. Turning the flag off again ended the incident.

The monthly path divides this month's spending total by the number of purchases made this month. Code-Fix's reading is that for a shopper who has bought before but not this month, that number is {F1.1}, so the division raises ZeroDivisionError. Code-Fix says the existing test helper calls this kind of shopper the ordinary case. Nothing ran this reading.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Turning on a new monthly-spending feature sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by the number of purchases made this month, and it likely broke for shoppers who had bought nothing yet this month.

contributing_factors.factor: Before the flag was switched on, no test or check was seen that ran the monthly spend summary for a shopper with no purchases this month. Code-Fix says its new tests for this case raise ZeroDivisionError against the current code.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been found before monthly-spend-feature reached shoppers, and the flag would not have been switched on with the fault still in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: No staged rollout or automatic hold on rising errors was seen for the flag change. Within the minute after the toggle, every evaluation of monthly-spend-feature came back on.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of shoppers would have reached the failing path, and the rise in errors could have stopped the rollout before it reached everyone.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

went_well: The Mitigation Agent turned monthly-spend-feature off {T18.1 - alert_raised} after the alert was raised, and it confirmed that the service was out of the incident's level.
The Investigator's single candidate pointed to the flag toggle, and turning the flag off confirmed it.
Code-Fix opened draft pull request #337, proposing a fix to the monthly average calculation together with new tests, {T23.1 - T22.1} after the incident was marked mitigated.

input.root_cause: The monthly spend summary works out average spend per item by dividing this month's spending total by the number of purchases made this month, with nothing guarding the case where that number is {F1.1}. Code-Fix's reading is that a shopper who has bought before but not this month gives that zero count, so the code raises ZeroDivisionError at src/io_shop/spend_summary.py line {F1.2} and the account page request fails.
input.still_at_risk: The calculation that divides by this month's purchase count is still in the code behind monthly-spend-feature, so switching the flag back on would likely make account pages fail again for shoppers with no purchases this month.
input.symptom: Account pages failed for many shoppers
